entry.title: Block-wide Signature Aggregation via SNARKs
entry.summary:
The discussion raises concerns about the suitability of BitVM in a specific context, emphasizing that Groth16, which it utilizes, is not quantum-secure and also necessitates a trusted setup, marking it as potentially unreliable for certain applications. Moreover, the mention of LeanVM introduces an alternative that could be more promising due to its novel attributes. Despite the acknowledged 10x performance overhead associated with LeanVM, the advantages it offers, such as portability and improved developer experience (DX), might outweigh the drawbacks if it proves to function effectively after thorough evaluation.
It is clear from the evaluation that while the integration of LeanVM seems appealing, the primary focus should lean towards efficiency and security rather than just enhancing portability and DX. The ongoing development and assessment of LeanVM will determine its feasibility in replacing or complementing current systems that rely on less secure or efficient frameworks like Groth16. This suggests a forward-looking approach in choosing the right virtual machine environment that aligns with specific security needs and performance criteria.
